proof_nl: Let x be any real number with 0 ≤ x. By the definition of the floor function, floor(x) is the greatest integer m such that m ≤ x. Since 0 is an integer and 0 ≤ x, the integer 0 is a candidate in this set. Therefore the greatest integer m ≤ x cannot be smaller than 0. Hence floor(x) ≥ 0.
solver_summary: If x is nonnegative, then 0 is an integer with 0 ≤ x. Since floor(x) is the greatest integer ≤ x, it must be at least 0.
vetter_reason: The proof correctly establishes the stated helper lemma: if x >= 0, then floor(x) >= 0, by using 0 as an integer candidate in the defining set of the floor. It is complete, matches the local semantic sketch, and introduces no dependency issues.
